This would make the south score 1 (as it is now), and the north score a 2 (which appears in one of the other statements). The qualifing factor here is the complex political geography, which is not refelected in the current scoring system at all. This complicates matters with regard to studying different tablets from different areas with their own political status - one cannot necessarily measure the entire TERR status of ED IIIa vs. all the tablets. It also raises issues with the CDLI period categoroes of course, and leads to a necessary covering each period group not just with scores, but also short historical-political summaries with maps that make it easy to connect the archives/city groups of texts we have with each scored entity. It will also uncover hidden issues with smaller text groups. There is a need to mitigate that with the zoom-out to periods like the CDLI does, and which allows for larger statistical analyses, but without loosing track of the fine details regarding each series of tablet collections.
